findings.title: extend() `if` changed to `while` reintroduces CVE-2018-17202 unbounded loop (CWE-835)
findings.description: The change replaces the JPEG EXTEND step (ITU-T T.81 Figure F.12) `if (v < vt)` with `while (v < vt)`. EXTEND must apply the offset once; a `while` loop re-executes indefinitely when the initial `v` is at or below the re-assigned bound. After the first iteration vt is fixed to (-1 << t) + 1, a negative constant, and `v += vt` makes v strictly smaller, so the condition `v < vt` never becomes false for sufficiently negative inputs (reachable via a crafted JPEG whose Huffman categories / `receive` accumulation yield large or sign-wrapped coefficient values). This is the exact inverse of the upstream fix 6a79d35d (CVE-2018-17202), and reintroduces a remotely triggerable decoder hang (DoS).
evidence: private int extend(int v, final int t) { int vt = (1 << (t - 1)); if/while (v < vt) { vt = (-1 << t) + 1; v += vt; } return v; }
extend() is invoked on JPEG DC/AC coefficients at lines 327 and 352 of JpegDecoder.java
findings.rule: CWE-835: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop'); CVE-2018-17202

resultText:
Based on my analysis, let me examine the key code section and its context thoroughly.

The change under review converts the `if` conditional in `JpegDecoder.extend()` into a `while` loop. I've verified the current state of the code at `JpegDecoder.java:400-408`, the call sites (`extend(diff, t)` at line 327 and `extend(zz[k], ssss)` at line 352), and the data flow through `receive()`/`JpegInputStream.nextBit()`.

This diff is the exact reverse of the upstream fix commit `6a79d35d` that resolved CVE-2018-17202 (CWE-835). The JPEG EXTEND algorithm (ITU-T T.81, Figure F.12) must apply the offset exactly once; replacing `if` with `while` re-introduces an unbounded loop: after the first pass `vt` becomes the fixed negative constant `(-1 << t) + 1` and `v += vt` strictly decreases `v`, so once `v` is at or below that bound the exit condition can never be satisfied. A crafted JPEG feeding negative/overflowed coefficient values (via the `receive` accumulation over many bits) reaches that state and hangs the decoder — a remotely triggerable denial of service.
